issues.legal_issue: A rent-control enactment that limits its application to transferred pending suits and proceedings does not apply to appeals already pending when it comes into force.
material_facts: A landlord’s possession suit was decreed before the rent-control enactment came into force.
The tenants’ appeal from that decree was pending when the enactment came into force.
The enactment’s transitional provision excluded appeals from the suits and proceedings transferred to courts under the enactment, and applied its provisions to those transferred matters.
issues.conclusion: The enactment did not apply to the pending appeal; the appeal was governed by the law in force when the decree was passed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 12 and 50 of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, read together, gave the enactment retrospective effect only to the extent expressly stated in section 50, namely for the suits and proceedings transferred under that section. Appeals were excluded. The Court approved the Full Bench ruling in Nilkanth v. Rasiklal (A.I.R. 1949 Bom. 210).

predicates.pending_appeal_at_commencement: A party had filed an appeal that remained pending when the new enactment came into force.
predicates.transitional_scope_excludes_appeals: The enactment’s transitional provision excluded appeals from the matters covered by its transfer arrangement.
predicates.new_law_applies_only_to_transferred_proc: The enactment made its provisions applicable to pending matters only when those matters were transferred under its transitional arrangement.

issues.definition: When an appeal is pending at commencement, the transitional provision excludes appeals, and the new law is confined to transferred proceedings, the appeal remains governed by the prior law.

issues.legal_issue: Provisions that address suits to be instituted after an enactment comes into force do not apply to suits already pending at that time.
material_facts: The landlord instituted the possession suit before the rent-control enactment came into force.
The suit had been decided at trial, and an appeal from the decree was pending, when the enactment came into force.
The tenant-protection provisions addressed suits to be instituted and referred to payment or tender at the hearing of such a suit.
issues.conclusion: The tenant-protection provisions concerning institution of suits and payment or tender at the hearing did not apply to suits already pending when the enactment came into force.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(2) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, refers to suits to be instituted after commencement; section 12(3), by referring to ‘such suit’, applies to the suits described in section 12(2). The Court held section 12 prospective, not retrospective, and agreed with the Full Bench in Nilkanth v. Rasiklal (A.I.R. 1949 Bom. 210).

predicates.landlord_tenant_possession_suit: A landlord brought a suit against a tenant seeking possession of premises.
predicates.suit_pending_at_commencement: The suit had not reached a final conclusion when the new enactment came into force.
predicates.provision_addresses_suits_to_be_institut: The provision describes suits to be instituted and links its protection to the hearing of such a suit.

issues.definition: A pending landlord-tenant possession suit does not receive protection under a provision framed for suits instituted after the enactment comes into force.
